function.name: game_board_analyser
function.description: Analyse a given board position of the game and suggest the optimal next move Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

game.description: The name of the game. In this case, chess

player.description: The current player whose turn is to move.

position.description: The current state of the board in FEN (Forsyth–Edwards Notation) format.

message.content: I’m not sure which chess tournament you’re referring to. Could you specify which event you mean (e.g., World Chess Championship, World Rapid, World Blitz, Chess Olympiad, Candidates Tournament, etc.)?
message.reasoning: The user asks: "Who won the chess tournament in 2015?" This is ambiguous: which chess tournament? Possibly the World Chess Championship 2015? That was held in 2015, but the winner was Magnus Carlsen? Actually, Magnus Carlsen defended his title against Sergey Karjakin in 2016. In 2015, there was no world championship. But there was the 2015 World Rapid Chess Championship, won by Magnus Carlsen. Or the 2015 World Blitz Chess Championship, won by Magnus Carlsen. Or the 2015 Chess Olympiad, won by Russia. Or the 2015 Candidates Tournament, won by Sergey Karjakin. The question is ambiguous. We need to ask clarifying question. According to policy, we should ask clarifying question.
